summary: The figure shows the changing composition of causes of death by WHO regions and globally from 2000 to 2048. Across all regions, the proportion of deaths due to communicable, maternal, perinatal, and nutritional conditions is projected to decline significantly, while noncommunicable diseases are expected to increase and become the dominant cause of death by 2048. Injuries remain relatively stable or slightly increase in some regions but constitute a smaller proportion compared to noncommunicable diseases. The African Region starts with the highest percentage of communicable diseases and shows the largest decline over time.
